props.title: Class of Nuke 'Em High

sections.content: Class of Nuke 'Em High (1986) perfectly embodies Troma Entertainment's signature blend of low-budget horror, social satire, and gleefully excessive gore. Set at Tromaville High School near a nuclear power plant, the film follows typical Troma tropes established in The Toxic Avenger (1984) - toxic waste mutations, over-the-top violence, and anti-corporate messaging wrapped in deliberately campy execution. Director Lloyd Kaufman crafts a wild ride that satirizes 1980s fears about nuclear power while incorporating elements of teen movies like Fast Times at Ridgemont High (1982) and The Breakfast Club (1985).

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond just Troma's catalogue. Its blend of body horror and high school drama paved the way for later teen horror-comedies like Night of the Creeps (1986) and Return of the Living Dead (1985). The practical effects, while crude by today's standards, showcase the DIY spirit that influenced independent filmmakers like Peter Jackson, whose early splatter films Bad Taste (1987) and Meet the Feebles (1989) share similar sensibilities. SUBHEAD: Nuclear Horror & Social Commentary

Class of Nuke 'Em High sits within a larger tradition of nuclear anxiety films from the 1980s. While big-budget productions like The Day After (1983) took serious approaches to nuclear fears, Troma's film uses exploitation cinema techniques to deliver similar messages. Its mutated students and corrupt officials mirror themes found in more "respectable" environmental horror films like C.H.U.D. (1984) and The Hills Have Eyes (1977), but with Troma's characteristic lack of subtlety.
